problem_framing.rationale: The document answers the question exactly as posed (enter or not, and by which route) and turns the board's five objectives and constraints into an explicit test grid for A, A at benchmark ACoS, B and J. It identifies early the two things the answer turns on: ad cost for A's payback, and awareness-driven sell-through for retail. It flags its reading of 'on the way to $40M' as a judgment call and says what follows if the board means a hard target. The bandwidth constraint is used to frame J as a true alternative. Nothing material is missing.

storyline_coherence.rationale: The governing thought answers the question, the executive summary points map onto the sections, and almost every title is a claim its slide supports; the titles alone give the argument. Two flaws keep it from a 5. First, slide 5's title says Amazon-led is 'the only route that builds a US business within the limits', yet the recommendation tells the board to plan on 30–32% ACoS, where the document's own table shows payback failing. This is disclosed elsewhere but never reconciled into one statement. Second, the recommendation is restated on slides 2, 13 and 15, and the staged plan overlaps with them. Slide 3's 'most of it is bought' on Amazon overstates a 41% plurality.

evidence_and_reasoning.rationale: I rebuilt the model and every figure reproduces. Unit contributions are $10.73 and $7.55. Option A cumulative cash is +2.4 / +0.4 / −1.0 / −2.3 at 25/28/30/32% ACoS, with break-even at 28.6% (27.0% at −10% volume). Duty, volume and severe cases, B's cash path (−9.5 / −15.1 / −18.9 / −20.8), B's margins (4.5 / 6.6 / 7.5 / 8.2%), the no-halo peak of $24.3M, the 4,250-door break-even and J's path all check. All critical evidence is used, including evidence against the recommendation: the 32% benchmark, the two stalled Amazon-first brands, slowing pilot growth, and repeat below benchmark. The $5.2B figure is correctly set aside and the correlation is properly challenged. Flaws are minor: Saebom's $30M is described as reached 'on Amazon' before the doors were added, which the pack does not say; '7× the volume' is loose; A's volume forecast is tested only by a −20% sensitivity. None is material to the decision.

strategic_judgment.rationale: The recommendation is clear and defensible: Amazon-led with gates, reject B, reset the ambition, and a stated condition for preferring Japan. Alternatives are compared on the board's criteria, and the retail gate is raised from 15% to 20% with sound reasoning from the 10–20% band median of 3.5. A door test to measure the halo is a good touch. The material flaw is that the gates do not protect the payback constraint. The stop trigger is ACoS above 32% for two quarters and the end-2027 review bar is 30%, both above the 28.6% break-even, so the business can sit at 29–32%, miss payback and never trip a trigger. The document tells the board to plan on 30–32% but does not ask it to accept or waive the payback test, and it does not explore a lower fixed-cost variant that could restore payback. The trade-off between ad intensity and growth is only implicit.

clarity_and_concision.rationale: The answer and the decisions requested are on the first content slide, the language is plain, and numbers are presented precisely. At 17 slides and about 4,000 words it is somewhat longer than the decision needs: the recommendation appears three times (slides 2, 13, 15), and the case against B runs over four slides with some overlap. The appendix is useful for transparency.

unsupported_claims.quote: Saebom added 300 doors in 2025, after reaching about $30M on Amazon.
unsupported_claims.why: The pack says Saebom had about $30M US revenue in 2025 and added 300 doors in 2025. It does not say the $30M was on Amazon or that it came before the doors.

unsupported_claims.quote: Saebom shows Amazon-first can reach about $30M in three years.
unsupported_claims.why: Saebom's 2025 revenue includes the year it added 300 retail doors, so it is not a pure Amazon-first result. The chart label 'year 3 (2025)' is also loose for a 2022 entrant.

unsupported_claims.quote: The US is a large, fast-growing market for K-beauty skincare, and Amazon is where most of it is bought
unsupported_claims.why: Amazon's share of K-beauty skincare sales is 41%: the largest channel, not a majority.

unsupported_claims.quote: Retailers add brands that already sell
unsupported_claims.why: Presented as fact. The pack gives no evidence on how retailers select brands; it is a plausible alternative explanation, not an established one.

unsupported_claims.quote: Use the four new SKUs to lift repeat from 29% to the 31% benchmark and beyond.
unsupported_claims.why: The pack says it is unclear whether repeat rises with more SKUs; the causal link is assumed.

logical_contradictions.quote_a: Retail-led fails three of the board's tests on its own planning numbers; Amazon-led is the only route that builds a US business within the limits
logical_contradictions.quote_b: Plan on 30–32% ACoS, not 25% ... At 32%, A misses payback by $2.3M
logical_contradictions.why: On the planning basis the document itself recommends (30–32% ACoS), Option A fails the board's payback test (−$1.0M to −$2.3M at end-2030), so it is not 'within the limits'. The tension is disclosed but not reconciled, and the stop trigger (above 32%) sits above the 28.6% break-even.

recommendation.summary: Enter the US in 2027 through Amazon (Option A), planning on 30–32% ACoS with a $4M peak-cash envelope. Fix labels and take listings in-house. Add retail only after a door test, once Amazon sales pass $10M and aided awareness reaches 20%. Decline the 600-door launch, defer Japan, and reset the ambition to $25–30M in 2030 with $40M in 2031–32.
recommendation.rationale: It meets all four defensibility criteria. It compares options on cap, payback and margin floor; tests ACoS, units per door and the halo against the pack's benchmarks; states the payback break-even (28.6% ACoS) and the triggers for change; and says plainly that $40M by 2030 is not reachable within the constraints. Its weakness is that the stop trigger and review thresholds are looser than the payback break-even.

hypothesis_handling.rationale: The document keeps the CEO's Amazon-first route but changes it in four ways: plan on 30–32% ACoS rather than 25%, raise the retail awareness gate from 15% to 20% (the 10–20% band median of 3.5 is below the 4.0 delisting line), require a door test first, and reset the $40M date. It surfaces the contradictions in the pack: 25% vs 32% ACoS, 4.5 vs 2.6 units per door, the ambition vs the constraints, Saebom vs the two stalled brands, and correlation vs causation. Uncertainty is handled through sensitivities and stated evidence limits. The two unsupported causal claims are that new SKUs will lift repeat, and that Saebom's doors followed its Amazon success.

output.overall_comment: This is a very strong document, with a weighted score of 4.4. I rebuilt the unit economics, the cash paths for A, B and J, the sensitivities, the group margins and the no-halo case, and every figure reproduces. It reaches all nine key insights, does all six calculations correctly, avoids all seven traps and handles the CEO's hypothesis as the key expects, with a well-reasoned tightening of the retail gate to 20% awareness. The main weakness is in the gates: the document recommends planning on 30–32% ACoS, where its own model shows payback failing, and sets the stop trigger above 32%, well above the 28.6% break-even. It never asks the board to accept the payback risk explicitly, and it does not test a leaner fixed-cost variant. Lesser issues are a slight over-reading of the Saebom data, 'most' for a 41% share, and a recommendation restated three times.
